## Conformance gap against a ratified ADR

ADR pm-irp1 (closed, "Accepted") decided cold-start is optimized by
"lazy-importing each command's own module through a thin dispatch layer in
src/cli/main.ts **rather than eagerly loading a single large command barrel**".

That barrel exists anyway, and it is src/sdk/runtime.ts.

## Measured evidence (2026-07-26, real workspace, 2,101 items)

Wall-clock, best of 3, warm:

| invocation | wall |
|---|---|
| pm --version (fast path, short-circuits before dispatch) | 73 ms |
| pm get pm-96h7 | 939 ms |
| pm list-open --limit 20 | 996 ms |
| pm search graph --limit 5 | 1156 ms |
| pm context --limit 5 | 1316 ms |
| pm next --limit 5 | 1381 ms |

Module-graph cost measured in isolation with a bare node import:

| module | import cost |
|---|---|
| node -e "" baseline | 44 ms |
| dist/sdk/runtime.js | **437 ms** |
| dist/sdk/index.js (barrel) | 462 ms |
| dist/cli/main.js | 459 ms |

So ~460 ms of every non-version invocation is module loading, and
**src/sdk/runtime.ts alone accounts for 437 ms of it**. pm get reports
profile:command=get took_ms=235 for the same invocation that costs 939 ms
wall — the unmeasured remainder is this import (see pm-ag9nka for why the
instrument cannot see it).

## Mechanism

- src/sdk/runtime.ts is 3,982 LOC, the largest file in the repository.
- It has **69 static imports and 0 dynamic imports**.
- It eagerly pulls every command implementation, including ones the current
  invocation cannot use: runTest + runTestAll (sdk/test/execution 155 ms,
  sdk/test/batch 156 ms), runInit (sdk/init 224 ms), runConfig, runTelemetry
  (72 ms), runDeps, runDocs, runFiles, runList.
- src/cli/main.ts contains **zero occurrences of "await import("** — the thin
  lazy dispatch layer the ADR specified was never built (or has regressed) —
  and it statically imports PmClient from ../sdk/runtime.js at main.ts:82.
- 15 modules statically import sdk/runtime.js, so no consumer can opt out.

Net effect: `pm get`, a single-item point read, pays for the linked-test
runner, the telemetry runtime, the workspace initializer and the extension
scaffolder before it reads one file.

## Why this is not an existing item

- pm-yse5dt (CLOSED) owned the per-invocation bootstrap *budget and gate*, and
  the CLI-minus-SDK transport delta. It measured the floor; it did not own the
  module that sets it.
- pm-38bskj (CLOSED) owned the *shape of the public SDK export surface*
  (881 exports, one flat entry). This is the CLI's internal command barrel, a
  different module and a different axis.
- pm-3mal (CLOSED) deferred three specific eager startup items (completion
  flag-strings, MCP tool schema build, telemetry flush spawn) — not the
  command-handler graph.
- pm-801d (open) is the data-scaling read index, orthogonal to transport.

This item owns the single mechanism: the eager command barrel that defeats
ADR pm-irp1, and the lazy dispatch layer that has to replace it.

## Direction (not a mandate for the fix)

Split runtime.ts so PmClient construction does not transitively require any
command handler; route handlers through per-command dynamic import in the
dispatch layer main.ts already owns; keep the public SDK surface unchanged so
this is a pure internal topology change. The 73 ms `--version` path already
proves the floor achievable once the barrel is off the critical path.
The eager command barrel in sdk/runtime.ts defeats ADR pm-irp1: 437ms of every invocation is module loading the command cannot use

src/cli/main.ts has zero dynamic imports and statically imports PmClient from sdk/runtime.ts, a 3,982-LOC barrel with 69 static imports and 0 dynamic imports that costs 437ms of the ~460ms every non---version pm invocation spends before doing any work.

src/cli/main.ts dispatches every command handler through a dynamic import rather than a static import of a command barrel; Importing the module that constructs PmClient no longer transitively loads runTest, runTestAll, runInit, runTelemetry, or the extension scaffolder; A cold-process measurement of a point read (pm get) on the live workspace shows total wall time reduced by at least the 437ms currently attributable to sdk/runtime.js import; The public SDK export surface and all documented subpath entrypoints are byte-identical before and after the split
Sub-second becomes sub-300ms for point reads
Restores the cold-start strategy the project already ratified, making every agent command feel instant instead of ~1s.
Every pm command on every host in every session pays this; it is the dominant term in the latency the user experiences as 'not instant'.
PmClient construction requires no command handler; per-command handlers load through dynamic import in the main.ts dispatch layer; public SDK surface unchanged.
Agents invoke pm hundreds of times per session; 437ms x every call is the single largest fixed cost in the tool, and the ADR that was supposed to prevent it is closed and Accepted.

message: Wire eager-barrel defect into the typed graph: implements the startup-latency ADR it violates, discovered from the earlier partial defer chore, related to the instrument that cannot measure it and the closed budget/shape owners.

value.text: A ratified, closed ADR is an audit oracle, not just a record. ADR pm-irp1 decided cold-start would be optimized by lazy per-command imports through a thin dispatch layer in src/cli/main.ts rather than a single large command barrel. Diffing that decision against the current tree found the barrel it forbade (src/sdk/runtime.ts, 3,982 LOC, 69 static imports, 0 dynamic imports) costing 437ms of every invocation, and main.ts containing zero dynamic imports. Neither the closed budget item pm-yse5dt nor the --profile instrument surfaced it: --profile starts inside the handler and reported 235ms for a 939ms pm get, and the budget item measured a floor without owning the module that sets it. The generalizable move is to treat every closed Decision as a conformance test against HEAD, because a decision that was never implemented leaves no failing test and no open item behind it.
